story.title: The Backup Life
story.logline: A man discovers he is only a clone kept in storage, activated solely when his primary self encounters fatal danger.
story.twist: His original self died yesterday, meaning he is no longer the backup—he is entirely alone.
story.ending: If I am the only one left, who keeps me in the dark?

scenes.narration: My heart stopped beating three minutes ago, and yet, here I am, waking up inside a freezing glass tube.
scenes.visual_prompt: 25-year-old male, messy dark hair, wearing a white utility jumpsuit, inside a glowing blue cryogenic pod, dark futuristic room
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up on terrified eyes, rapidly zooming out

scenes.narration: The emergency lights pulse red, casting harsh shadows across the sterile walls of the underground activation chamber I call home.
scenes.visual_prompt: 25-year-old male, messy dark hair, white jumpsuit, standing in a sterile glowing subterranean chamber with red emergency lights

scenes.narration: A digital screen flashes my exact serial number. I am not a person. I am a reserve body, waiting for a crash.
scenes.visual_prompt: 25-year-old male, messy dark hair, white jumpsuit, staring at a floating holographic screen displaying clone serial numbers

scenes.narration: Every memory in my head belongs to him. The coffee shops, the heartbreaks, the laughs. They were all just downloaded.
scenes.visual_prompt: 25-year-old male, messy dark hair, white jumpsuit, touching his head with a pained expression in the dim room

scenes.narration: My primary self was supposed to survive his mountain climb today. That is the only reason my pod was programmed to open.
scenes.visual_prompt: 25-year-old male, messy dark hair, white jumpsuit, looking up at a status monitor showing a mountain hiking trail map

scenes.narration: I press my palm against the heavy steel exit door, expecting it to remain locked until the system syncs our lives.
scenes.visual_prompt: 25-year-old male, messy dark hair, white jumpsuit, pressing his bare hand against a massive scratched steel bulkhead door
scenes.camera: Medium tight shot on hands and door

scenes.narration: The door slides open with a hiss, spilling golden morning sunlight onto my bare feet for the very first time.
scenes.visual_prompt: 25-year-old male, messy dark hair, white jumpsuit, stepping through a heavy door into blinding golden morning sunlight outside

scenes.narration: I step out onto the quiet forest trail, ready to finally take over his life and live freely under the sun.
scenes.visual_prompt: 25-year-old male, messy dark hair, white jumpsuit, walking onto a green pine tree forest path, breathing deeply

scenes.narration: Then my wrist implant buzzes. A red notification reads: Primary signal lost permanently. Signal flatline confirmed at dawn.
scenes.visual_prompt: 25-year-old male, messy dark hair, white jumpsuit, staring down at a glowing red text prompt flashing on his wrist skin
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up on wrist and glowing text

scenes.narration: If the original is truly gone forever, then who exactly am I backing up now?
scenes.visual_prompt: 25-year-old male, messy dark hair, white jumpsuit, standing alone in the vast empty forest, looking straight into the lens
scenes.camera: Slow push-in to a haunting close-up

caption.hook: I was only built to die for him.
caption.title: The Backup Life
caption.caption:
For my whole existence, I slept in the dark, waiting for my primary to bleed. But yesterday, the monitor flatlined permanently, leaving me awake in a world that was never meant to be mine. What happens when the spare finally has to live?

If you were the backup, would you try to play the lead?
